simple.meaning: חֹמֶט (chômeṭ) is a Hebrew word meaning “a lizard (as creeping).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This word has limited occurrence data, so BibleIQ begins with the Hebrew word, its basic meaning, and the verse where it appears.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֹמֶט (H2546) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חֹמֶט (H2546) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חֹמֶט (chômeṭ) / H2546 is traced through Leviticus 11:30 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H2546. chomet חֹ֫מֶט noun [masculine] a kind of lizard , only in list of unclean creeping animals Lev 11:30 ׃ וְהַתִּנְשָֽׁמֶת וְהַחֹמֶט וְהַלְּטָאָ֑ה וְהַכֹּחַ וְהָאֲנָקָה (Aramaic is chameleon ).
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root probably meaning, to lie low;

occurrences.englishText: the gecko, and the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
